result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers trace the generic look to the same stacked category defaults, and both flag the tagline and fine details failing at avatar and sign sizes. B commits to one direction rooted in the name (a custom ampersand) and keeps the brown, pink, gold and tagline in reduced roles. A offers a menu of options, tells the bakery to drop the whole palette, keeps almost nothing, and ends on a longer list of equal steps. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain clearly why the logo looks generic, and B is somewhat stronger on how it holds up at small sizes and in one colour. A commits to one concrete idea rooted in the name: a custom ampersand. It keeps the dark brown, moves pink and gold to accents and gives tight next steps. B spreads across six equal changes and throws out nearly every existing element, including all current colours and the script, so it reads closer to a blanket rejection.
